findings.title: Partition lock creation is racy, breaks offset mutual exclusion
findings.body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock reads/writes self.partition_locks dict with no global lock. Two threads creating a lock for the same new Partition can each create a different threading.Lock via setdefault race, so add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable/mark_committed for that partition then synchronize on different locks. get_committable also does list(self.all_offsets.keys()) while add_offset can mutate the dict, risking RuntimeError or missed partitions. Consequence is corrupted outstanding/all_offsets sets and wrong committable offsets (duplicate processing or stalled commits).

findings.title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure, risk OOM
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() never blocks, while SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit/poll never apply backpressure. The docstring claims natural backpressure when queues fill up, but queues never fill. A slow group_key lets the consumer keep polling Kafka and enqueueing unbounded WorkItems (which retain full Message payloads), growing memory until OOM. qsize-based stats/metrics also under-report because qsize drops on get() before processing finishes.

findings.title: Failed items are marked complete and committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. The strategy docstring claims only commits offsets after successful processing, but failures become committable and are committed by the commit loop, bypassing retry and Arroyo DLQ handling. A transient DB error or bug in handle_result is silently skipped and the Kafka offset advances, losing the result forever.

findings.title: Shared queue pool is shut down by per-partition strategy close
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ shared by every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate calls self.queue_pool.shutdown(). On rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy, which sets worker.shutdown=True and shuts down queues used by the new strategy, discarding queued work and stopping workers. Multiple strategies also each spawn a commit thread sharing one OffsetTracker but committing via different commit closures, causing duplicate or partition-incorrect commits.

findings.title: Shutdown discards queued but unprocessed items
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before draining, and OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on while not self.shutdown. After finishing the current item a worker exits even if its queue still holds items. Those WorkItems were already add_offset-tracked but never complete_offset, so close/join does not flush them. Combined with use of queue.Queue.shutdown/queue.ShutDown (Python 3.13+ only), on older runtimes q.shutdown raises AttributeError which is swallowed, leaving workers blocked on get() forever and join() timing out with leaked daemon threads.
